subject: sociology
intro: Sociology leads to paid work that studies, measures and mends social life — from research teams who survey whole populations to probation officers and community programmes that work with people one by one.

roles.title: Sociologists
roles.what: Study human society and social behaviour by examining the groups, institutions and organisations people form — religious, political and business bodies alike — and research how individuals move and act within them.
roles.where: The research-methods unit trains the craft of investigating society; the stratification and inequality units give you the substantive questions; lessons on class, gender and race-and-ethnicity supply the concepts professional sociologists apply daily.

roles.title: Survey Researchers
roles.what: Plan, develop and conduct surveys: decide what to ask and of whom, design and test question wording, then analyse and interpret the data the answers produce for clients and policymakers.
roles.where: Unit 1 — research methods — is this job in miniature: the types of data sociologists use, how they questionnaires and samples, and how they read the evidence afterwards all come straight from that syllabus topic.

roles.title: Probation Officers and Correctional Treatment Specialists
roles.what: Provide social services that help rehabilitate law offenders in custody or on probation or parole, drawing up treatment plans and recommending to courts how each person should be supervised and supported.
roles.where: The crime, deviance and social control unit — what counts as crime, the patterns behind it and how different societies deal with it — is the theory base these officers apply when assessing people and proposing rehabilitation plans.

roles.title: Social and Community Service Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate the programmes of social service and community outreach organisations — supervising staff, administering budgets and shaping the policies that decide who the programme serves and how.
roles.where: The stratification unit's topic on attempts to reduce social inequalities maps onto programme design, while the family and education units ground you in the communities these managers organise services around.

roles.title: Sociology Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach sociology courses at colleges and universities — lecturing on social theory, inequality and research practice, designing assessments, and often combining teaching with their own published research.
roles.where: Every unit you study here is material a future lecturer teaches: the identity and socialisation lessons, Marx-to-Bourdieu social theory and the demography unit are all staple content of undergraduate sociology degrees.
